units: <cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 8:19">Tosef. B. Kam. VIII, 19</cite>. Mekh. Mishp., Nzikin, s. 7 (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 21:26">Ex. XXI, 26</cite>) <he>בכ׳ וכ׳</he> the text speaks of a Canaanite slave, opp. to <he>עבד עברי</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 1:3">Kidd. I, 3</cite> <he>עבד כ׳ נקנה וכ׳</he> a Canaanite slave is taken possession of &c.; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="K00870"><he>כְּנַעֲנִים</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 9:10">Tosef. B. Kam. IX, 10</cite>. Mekh. l. c. s. 3 <he>כדרך שהכ׳ וכ׳</he> as the Canaanite slaves go free.
<cite ref="Sotah 35b:13">Sot. 35ᵇ</cite> <he>כ׳ שבח״ל</he> Canaanites outside of Palestine.

<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 306:20">Sifré Deut. 306</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 942:19">Yalk. ib. 942</cite> (ref. to <he>יערף</he>, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 32:2">Deut. XXXII, 2</cite>) <he>לשון כ׳ וכ׳</he> it is a merchant’s expression, f. i., a man says not to his neighbor, ‘change for me &c.,’ but ‘break &c.’ <he>(ערוף</he>).
